plain.text: Some time later God tested Abraham. "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the region of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains." Early the next morning Abraham set out with Isaac, two servants and wood for the offering. On the third day they saw the place in the distance. Abraham told the servants, "Stay here. The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will come back to you." Isaac carried the wood. He asked, "Father, the fire and wood are here, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?" Abraham answered, "God himself will provide the lamb, my son." At the place, Abraham built an altar, arranged the wood, bound Isaac and laid him on the altar. He took the knife to slay his son.

But the angel of the LORD called from heaven, "Abraham, Abraham! Do not lay a hand on the boy. Now I know that you fear God, because you have not withheld your only son from me." Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He offered the ram instead of his son. Abraham called the place "The LORD Will Provide". The angel spoke again: because Abraham had not withheld his only son, God would bless him, make his descendants as many as the stars and the sand, and through his offspring all nations of the earth would be blessed, because he had obeyed. They returned to Beersheba.
Later, Abraham was told that his brother Nahor had children, including Bethuel, the father of Rebekah.

summary.bigIdea: God tests Abraham's trust, stops him from harming Isaac, and provides a ram instead: "The LORD will provide."
points: God asks Abraham to offer Isaac, the son of the promise.
Abraham trusts: "God himself will provide the lamb."
God stops him and provides a ram; Abraham names the place "The LORD Will Provide".
summary.reflection: This is a hard and troubling story. What questions does it raise for you, and what does it show about trust?
